correctness.rationale: For the uniform Dirichlet vector the kth projected moment is 6 k!/(k+3)! times the complete homogeneous polynomial in the four knots. The divided difference of the exponential gives exactly the sine quotient, whose canceled origin has value 1. The order-at-most-one real entire numerator with all real zeros has a real genus-at-most-one Hadamard product and is in the Laguerre–Pólya class. At x=2 pi/(1-a) its Laguerre defect is -a(1-a)^2 sin^2(x), forcing 2/(1-a) to be integral. Conversely, for m>=3 the numerator with z=mw is sin(w) Q_m(cos w)/m. Independently, Q_m(x)=2(1-x^2) U'_{m-2}(x) by differentiating sin((m-1)w)/sin(w); Rolle's theorem and the degree show that all m-3 derivative roots are simple and interior, with simple endpoint factors. Cosine preimages of [-1,1] are real. Interior factors give simple zeros and the endpoint factors combine with sin(w) to give triple zeros at w=k pi, including the canceled origin. The same Hadamard argument applies to the real entire quotient for the Laguerre–Pólya assertion. Record's script and output inspected, not executed. Independent bounded checks of the divided difference, factorization and root counts for m=3..20, and a negative defect at a=1/4: python3 /workspace/reproductions/independent_checks.py 1. The universal proof is analytic; it does not locate every nonreal zero in the nonexceptional cases.

evidence: Pham–Stefanov count real roots with algebraic multiplicity and count all roots in the right half-plane; their counts enforce infinitely many nonreal roots off the exceptional ratios. Proposition 2.2 identifies triple zeros as the common zeros of the two sines and absence of other multiple roots.

Adams–Cardon's Hermite–Biehler exponential-sum construction and Cardon's Rademacher-based Fourier theorem supply sufficient mechanisms under other hypotheses. Cardon's Laguerre inequalities supply the general criterion used by the frozen elementary necessity proof.

evidence: Pham–Stefanov's count difference is positive for irrational gamma in (0,1) and rational p/q with p>1. At gamma=1/q it is o(r); any nonreal root would replicate under shifts q pi since F_gamma(t+q pi)=(-1)^(q+1)F_gamma(t), giving linear growth of the nonreal count, a contradiction.

At 1/q the identity F_(1/q)(q w)=sin^3(w) U'_(q-1)(cos w)/q recovers the explicit zero set by elementary Chebyshev differentiation. The Laguerre–Pólya assertion adds no restriction beyond reality for this order-at-most-one real entire quotient.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The zero-density case is not misquoted as proving no nonreal roots by itself; periodic translation is necessary for that inference. The zero-classification, multiplicities and Laguerre–Pólya version follow after that step and standard factorization. The divided-difference representation and its Dirichlet spline interpretation are classical.

evidence: Eq. (7) of arXiv:1309.3616v2 gives F_gamma(t)=gamma sin(t) cos(gamma t)-sin(gamma t) cos(t). With z=(1+gamma)t and a=(1-gamma)/(1+gamma), this is (1+gamma)/2 times sin(az)-a sin(z). The exceptional 1/gamma integer is exactly m=1+1/gamma.

originality.rationale: The nonzero-zero problem is exactly the constant-index one-dimensional transmission eigenvalue problem of Pham and Stefanov (2013/2014), not merely an analogue. Their all-root and real-root counts give the necessity and, by period translation at the exceptional rational ratios, sufficiency; they also give the simple/triple split. The Chebyshev restatement and transfer to this simplex transform require standard identities. The exact theorem is covered even though the geometric language and proof are different.
residual_risks: No conclusion on priority for the shorter one-point Laguerre-inequality proof or whether an earlier simplex-specific phrasing exists.
The prior complex count is asymptotic, not an exact finite complex zero enumeration; that distinction does not affect the all-real classification.

value.rationale: The rigidity theorem concerns a natural projection family and the elementary proof is a useful exposition. But the advertised exact zero classification transfers directly from the earlier determinant via scaling and classical identities. The geometric reformulation introduces no additional zero invariant or nontrivial inference about projections beyond that translation, so it does not survive as a separate scientific finding under the stated standard.
